description:
## Why

The CompositeBlockStore (stoa-wqxq6) uses a global write_policy (all vs. primary). This is too coarse when multiple instances of the same backend type are configured with different credentials or access levels.

The concrete use case: an operator points stoa at 3 S3 buckets — their own (writable) and two peers' buckets (read-only, either public or with read-only credentials). Reads waterfall across all three. Writes go only to the operator's own bucket. No local copying of peer articles needed — stoa serves them directly from the source bucket.

This is a natural fit for NNTP peering: each peer exposes their block store (S3 bucket, WebDAV endpoint, public fs mount) and you read from all of them while writing only to your own.

## What

Add a per-backend `writable` boolean flag (default: true) to each [[backend]] entry in the config. The CompositeBlockStore read policy (first_found) is unchanged. The write policy ignores any backend with `writable = false`.

Example config:
```toml
[[backend]]
type = "s3"
bucket = "my-primary"
writable = true

[[backend]]
type = "s3"
bucket = "peer-a-blocks"
writable = false

[[backend]]
type = "s3"
bucket = "peer-b-blocks"
writable = false
```

## Design

- Reads: try all backends in declaration order, return first hit regardless of writable flag.
- Writes: put only to backends where writable = true. If no writable backend is configured, return a clear config error at startup rather than silently dropping writes.
- Deletes: only from writable backends.
- Validation at startup: warn if more than one backend has writable = true (ambiguous write target); error if zero backends have writable = true.
- Single-backend configs with no writable field default to writable = true (backward compatible).

## Acceptance

- writable = false backends are skipped on put and delete
- writable = false backends are included in the read waterfall
- Zero writable backends is a startup config error
- Single-backend config with no writable field continues to work unchanged
- Tests cover: write goes only to writable backends, read falls through to read-only backends, zero-writable-backends startup error
notes: The NNTP peering use case (read from peers' buckets, write only to your own) is the primary motivation. Consider whether peer bucket credentials should live in the [peers] config section rather than [[backend]] to keep the separation clean.
title: Per-instance writable flag for composite backend
